articles.body: 블록체인 혁명은 전례 없는 탈중앙화와 불변성을 약속했지만, 주류 채택을 가로막는 근본적인 난관에 봉착해왔다. 그중에서도 가장 큰 문제는 확장성, 보안성, 탈중앙화를 동시에 달성하기 어려운 '블록체인 트릴레마'다. 더불어 거래 프라이버시의 지속적인 부재와 서로 다른 네트워크 간의 단편화된 상호운용성도 큰 걸림돌이었다. 이러한 한계는 네트워크 혼잡, 엄청난 거래 수수료, 민감한 금융 데이터의 공개 노출, 그리고 블록체인 간의 '고립된 정원' 효과를 초래했다. 이때 영지식 증명(Zero-Knowledge Proofs, ZK-proofs)이라는 혁신적인 암호화 기술이 강력한 변화의 동력으로 급부상하고 있다. ZK-proof는 본질적으로 한 당사자(증명자)가 다른 당사자(검증자)에게 특정 주장이 사실임을 증명할 수 있게 한다. 이때 증명자는 그 주장이 사실이라는 정보 외에 어떠한 다른 정보도 노출하지 않는다. 마치 생년월일을 밝히지 않고 18세 이상임을 증명하거나, 비밀 키 자체를 공개하지 않고 소유권을 입증하는 것과 같다. 한때 이론적인 암호학의 영역에 머물렀던 이 마법 같은 기능은 이제 실용적인 블록체인 솔루션으로 정교하게 구현되며, 블록체인 생태계를 근본적으로 재편할 잠재력을 보여준다. 이 글은 10년간의 암호화폐 및 블록체인 연구 경험을 바탕으로, ZK-proof가 기존 블록체인 패러다임을 단순히 최적화하는 것을 넘어, 전례 없는 확장성, 견고한 프라이버시, 그리고 유기적인 상호운용성을 특징으로 하는 차세대 탈중앙화 시스템을 어떻게 촉진하는지 심층적으로 다룰 예정이다.

articles.title: How to Find and Fix Memory Leaks in .NET Projects
articles.excerpt: Memory leaks in .NET applications can be confusing. After all, .NET has a Garbage Collector (GC) that automatically removes objects that are no longer needed. So developers often ask: “If .NET has gar…
articles.body: Memory leaks in .NET applications can be confusing. After all, .NET has a Garbage Collector (GC) that automatically removes objects that are no longer needed. So developers often ask: “If .NET has garbage collection, how can a memory leak happen?” The answer is that the Garbage Collector can only collect objects that are no longer reachable . If an object is still referenced somewhere in your application—even accidentally—the GC considers it alive and cannot reclaim its memory. This article presents a practical workflow for finding memory leaks in .NET applications using tools such as dotnet-counters , dotnet-dump , and dotnet-gcdump . What Is a Memory Leak in .NET? A memory leak in .NET usually doesn't mean that memory is completely lost forever.

articles.title: What Is Decisioning Infrastructure for Consumer Platforms?
articles.excerpt: Consumer platforms make thousands or millions of decisions every second about what users see. A social platform decides which posts appear in a feed. A marketplace decides which listings appear first.…
articles.body: Consumer platforms make thousands or millions of decisions every second about what users see. A social platform decides which posts appear in a feed. A marketplace decides which listings appear first. A creator platform decides which creators or content to recommend. A dating app decides which profiles to surface. A job board decides which jobs should appear at the top of a candidate's search. Behind all of these experiences is a common technical problem: given a set of possible items, which items should be shown, in what order, and under what business rules? Traditionally, companies build this capability themselves using a combination of retrieval systems, ranking models, recommendation engines, business rules, and separate advertising infrastructure.

articles.title: UI Architecture That AI Coding Agents Can Actually Use
articles.excerpt: When we ask an AI agent to "add a confirmation modal before deleting a user," we expect a focused pull request. What we usually get is an archaeological expedition. Without clear module boundaries, th…
articles.body: When we ask an AI agent to "add a confirmation modal before deleting a user," we expect a focused pull request. What we usually get is an archaeological expedition. Without clear module boundaries, the agent's first job is excavation: deciphering undocumented state, tracing network calls across files, and guessing where UI decisions belong. It imports a global store here, tweaks a shared utility there, and produces a sprawling diff that touches unrelated files. The problem isn't the model's reasoning. It's that the codebase gives it infinite room to wander. A bounded perimeter An agent needs to know where its task begins and, crucially, where it stops. In a tangled codebase, a simple visual adjustment can cascade into root layouts, authentication guards, and global routers.

articles.title: Zet: an open-source layer on Laya that knows when to ask a human
articles.excerpt: Confidence scores aren't error rates. Zet sits on top of Laya and marks every answer sure or unsure, using conformal prediction sets and a Learn-then-Test threshold calibrated per language, so the ans…
articles.body: Confidence scores aren't error rates. Zet sits on top of Laya and marks every answer sure or unsure, using conformal prediction sets and a Learn-then-Test threshold calibrated per language, so the answers it automates stay within an error budget you choose (say 5%). On MASSIVE (human-labeled, 300 examples per language, 5% budget), it automated 84% of English and 80% of Swedish requests on a 6-scenario task, with 0 errors in 75 sure English answers. When the task got harder (18 scenarios), it automated nothing, while its prediction sets still contained the right answer 97-99% of the time. That refusal is the feature working. Runs locally on ONNX Runtime with no PyTorch, with a web interface for creating tasks, uploading labeled examples, calibrating, and reviewing unsure answers.

articles.body: Diablo 4 director Brent Gibson is telling fans not to worry about the game after Diablo 5’s announcement sparked concerns about the former title’s lifespan. Diablo 5’s reveal at Blizzcon 2026 left fans equal parts excited and worried. Of course, players were pumped for a new Diablo game — but with Diablo 4 having just launched in 2023, the reveal of a new game so soon felt like a death knell for the one they were still playing. But Brent Gibson, director of Diablo 4, says there’s nothing to fuss about. Speaking with Icy Veins , Gibson outlined some plans for the game’s future content, saying it will continue to receive support well after 5’s release. “I have an analogy,” he began. “If you’re wearing a sign in the middle of Times Square saying, ‘The end is nigh,’ the end is not nigh.

Ariel Lawrence has been with the God of War franchise since its very first game — but creator David Jaffe, who left the series behind in 2007 to form his own studio, says he never got along with her during his time at Santa Monica Studio. articles.body: Elon Musk | Image: Laura Normand / The Verge Grokipedia, the AI-powered online encyclopedia from SpaceXAI, appears to be updating articles once again after a months-long pause . articles.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6.1 Sol with Astra-like performance on a budget
articles.excerpt: Access gets started with ChatGPT Work and Codex, but Chat will have to wait.
articles.body: TL;DR OpenAI is introducing GPT-6.1 Sol, promising Astra-like performance at one-fifth the expenditure. Across numerous benchmarks, GPT-6.1 Sol comes close to 6 Astra’s capabilities, and outpaces GPT-6 Sol. GPT-6.1 demonstrates fewer factual errors than GPT-6 Sol across similar tests. DevDay is here for OpenAI, and that means the company is sharing a whole bunch of news about its latest work on models and the services built around them. While we just heard that GPT-6.1 Astra is getting sent back to the bench for misbehaving, progress continues on the rest of OpenAI’s headlining models, and this afternoon we’re getting the scoop on the first member of that 6.1-series to actually make its public debut, with the launch of GPT‑6.1 Sol.
